cells.tense: Right now you're the one deciding what this moment is for, out loud.
cells.ask: Get two or three people talking about what one shared thing means to each of them, and keep your own answer to a sentence or two.
cells.core:
The room tilts a little when you put a feeling on the table, and people lean in. That's what you're good at. You bring a charge and you mean it to land somewhere real, so what you say settles into how people stand with each other for hours after.

Under this, the fair thing is still being weighed in real time — what you give, what comes back, who gets left out. Your part is to keep that scale honest while something real is moving. That is the shape of this, and it's a good one. One true sentence does more work than four careful ones, and in your hands that's usually right. Hand it to the two or three who are actually here.
cells.sheetLine: You make it land, and you're not pretending you don't.
cells.verb: Making shared meaning land through feeling
cells.place: Where what is fair between people is weighed and set right

cells.tense: You're already feeling how this should land before anyone's in the room to receive it.
cells.ask: Name the exchange in front of you as just an exchange, out loud, and let the other person say how it's going.
cells.core:
You can feel the perfect version of this forming ahead of time — the words that land, the tone that moves, the moment people come together. The gap between that version and the one happening now is what's driving you tonight, and you're pushing toward the one that isn't here yet.

Every exchange is being measured before it's even had. That's the part costing you — the weighing has stopped being shared, so you do it alone, in advance. The fair version only turns up when the other person gets to shape it too. What you're best at is water, not stone. It waits for the actual shape of the glass, and each glass is different. Let this one in, and let the person across from you set the current.

cells.tense: You used to put a feeling into a room and it changed something; you haven't tried that in a while.
cells.ask: Put one true sentence about what something means to you in front of someone, without moving them with it.
cells.core:
Somewhere back there you stopped being the one who puts a feeling on the table. Maybe it went badly, maybe it was taken the wrong way, maybe you just got tired. However it went, the scale you trust has been running on other people's weights since then — careful, even, fair on the surface, and cool all the way through.

The charge is still in you. The touch that turns it into something shared is what quit. And pushing harder into the quiet part won't bring it back. Set up one small exchange where the fair weight is checked out loud — what each person gives and takes. A plain trade first, then a real one. You're still the one who can make meaning land. Nothing there has gone.

cells.tense: You're already the one naming what this moment means, and you call it just going along with the room.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, 'I'm the one making this land,' about a moment you thought was happening by itself.
cells.core:
When you're in a group, you say the sentence that names what this is — the joke that sets the tone, the question that turns it real, the line people repeat after. The moment looks like it shaped itself. That's you doing it, and you keep describing yourself as easygoing.

It's not a small thing. At the moment when the fair thing between people is being weighed, you're one of the ones with a hand on the scale, and you've been saying otherwise for a while now. The influence is running. The word for it has not been said. One sentence, said to yourself first. You already have the proof of it.
